The Russo-Japanese War (1904-1905) was fought over imperial ambitions in Korea and Manchuria, with Russia seeking a year-round warm-water port.
Japan, an emerging military power, decisively defeated the larger Russian forces on land and sea. Key victories included the Siege of Port Arthur, the Battle of Mukden, and the naval Battle of Tsushima.
The war ended with the Treaty of Portsmouth in 1905, brokered by US President Theodore Roosevelt.
